The objective of this project is to deploy a secure, scalable and high-performance enterprise network and data
center infrastructure for Dawood University of Engineering & Technology, enabling centralized monitoring,
seamless connectivity and efficient IT operations. The proposed solution incorporates next-generation firewall
security to ensure robust protection against network threats and secure access to critical resources. A
centralized network management and orchestration platform, aligned with Software-Defined Networking (SDN)
architecture, will enable simplified configuration, monitoring, automation and overall network administration.
Wireless connectivity across the facility will be enabled using next-generation Wi-Fi access points, including both
indoor and outdoor models, ensuring seamless wireless coverage and high-speed connectivity throughout the
campus. The project also includes the deployment of a fully equipped data center environment comprising
communication racks, structured cabling, environmental monitoring, fire suppression, access control, CCTV
surveillance and uninterrupted power systems.
All components will operate under a unified management framework, enabling centralized visibility and control.
The project will be delivered as a turnkey solution, including supply, installation, configuration, testing,
commissioning and final handover.
5. Scope of Work
The scope of work includes the supply, installation, configuration and support of modern enterprise network
and data center infrastructure to ensure secure connectivity, centralized monitoring and high-performance
communication across the DUET. The project involves the implementation of Huawei USG6625F next-generation
firewalls to provide comprehensive network security and protection against threats. Centralized network
management will be implemented through Huawei iMaster NCE-Campus, enabling a Software Defined
Networking (SDN) architecture for simplified configuration, monitoring and management.
The access network will be established using Huawei CloudEngine S5735-L series switches with multi-gigabit and
Power over Ethernet (PoE+) capabilities to support end-user devices and provide high-speed uplink connectivity.
Wireless connectivity will be delivered through Huawei AirEngine Wi-Fi 7 access points, including both indoor
and outdoor models, to ensure seamless and high-speed wireless c

The network will be deployed based on a Software Defined Networking (SDN) architecture, centrally managed
via the Huawei iMaster NCE-Campus controller. The NETS International will be responsible for the installation,
configuration and integration of the SDN controller to manage all networking devices. This includes centralized
configuration, monitoring, policy enforcement and real-time troubleshooting of firewalls, switches and wireless
access points. The SDN architecture will support 802.1X authentication to ensure secure device access and will
provide a unified interface for administrators to manage the complete network infrastructure.

Huawei USG6625F next-generation firewalls will be deployed to secure the network infrastructure. The NETS
International will handle the installation, configuration and integration of all firewall devices, including license
activation and connectivity to the SDN controller. Firewalls will provide advanced security features such as
stateful inspection, intrusion prevention, antivirus and URL filtering. They will be configured to enforce
consistent security policies across the organization and integrated with the SDN platform to enable centralized
monitoring and management.

The access network layer will be implemented using Huawei CloudEngine S5735-L series switches. The NETS
International will manage the installation and configuration of these switches, including physical mounting in
racks, cable terminations, port configurations, VLANs and connectivity with the SDN controller. These switches
will deliver high-speed connectivity, PoE+ support for connected devices and Layer-2/Layer-3 routing
capabilities, ensuring robust and reliable network performance.

The wireless network will be established using Huawei AirEngine Wi-Fi 7 access points, including both indoor and
outdoor models. The NETS International will perform the installation and configuration of all access points,
ensuring full coverage, optimal channel allocation and seamless roaming capabilities. Wireless devices will be
configured and integrated with the SDN controller for centralized monitoring, management and security
enforcement. This ensures high-capacity, secure and reliable wireless connectivity throughout the DUET’s
facilities.
NETS International will use the existing structured cabling already installed at the site. The Cat6A cables for Wi-Fi
7 access points are already available at current locations, so these will be reused for installing the new Wi-Fi 7
access points. At existing access points locations, only the devices will be replaced or upgraded and no new
cabling work will be required.
For any new access point locations identified during the survey (approximately 10-15 units), NETS International
will provide and install Cat6A cabling, including all necessary items such as patch cords, connectors and labeling
to ensure proper connectivity and performance.
Furthermore, it is understood that the existing access points placement is already optimized and there are no
wireless coverage issues. Therefore, no wireless heat map would be provided as part of this project. The new
Wi-Fi 7 access points will be installed at the same validated locations to maintain consistent and reliable wireless
performance.

9

The project includes the construction and setup of a dedicated data center facility designed to support the
DUET’s critical IT infrastructure. The data center will include communication racks for mounting network
equipment and servers, along with structured cabling systems that organize network connections efficiently.
Additional infrastructure will include fiber patch panels, cable management systems and environmental
monitoring systems to ensure stable operating conditions. Fire suppression systems using FM-200 gas will be
installed to protect equipment from fire hazards without causing damage to electronic components. The facility
will also include CCTV monitoring systems and access control mechanisms to ensure physical security and
controlled access to the data center environment.
The NETS International will utilize existing FM-200 fire suppression system. As part of the project scope, the
NETS International will carry out inspection and refilling of the FM-200 system, as mutually agreed during the
site survey, to ensure it is fully operational and compliant with safety requirements.
Additionally, the existing earthing (grounding) system will be utilized for the data center and network
infrastructure. The NETS International will assess the current earthing system and perform necessary
rectification, strengthening, or revival wherever deficiencies are identified to ensure proper grounding and
equipment safety.

A complete electrical distribution system will be installed to support the data center and networking equipment.
This includes power distribution boards, electrical wiring and power cabling designed to deliver stable and
reliable electrical supply to all critical infrastructure components. The power infrastructure will also include
uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems that provide backup power during outages or fluctuations. These
UPS systems will ensure continuous operation of critical network equipment and prevent data loss or service
disruptions. Additional electrical installations will include LED lighting fixtures, industrial power sockets and
supporting electrical accessories required for the safe and efficient operation of the facility.

To maintain stable operating conditions, the NETS International will supply, install and configure cooling
systems including split inverter air conditioners and floor-standing AC units. Proper installation of piping,
drainage and airflow management will ensure optimal temperature and humidity levels within the data center.
The cooling infrastructure will be integrated with environmental monitoring systems for real-time observation
and control.
The data center cooling system will be configured to operate on an automatic switching mechanism to ensure
continuous and efficient temperature control. The installed air conditioning units will function in a manner that
allows automatic changeover between units, ensuring redundancy and maintaining optimal environmental
conditions within the data center without manual intervention.

The NETS International will provide complete structured cabling system, including Cat6A copper cables, patch
panels, patch cords, cable trays and labeling. All cabling will be organized and terminated according to industry
best practices to ensure high performance, reliability and ease of maintenance. The cabling system will support
high-speed communication and future scalability.

All deployed components will be fully integrated into a unified solution. The NETS International will perform
installation, configuration, integration and commissioning of all hardware and software. This includes end-to-
end connectivity testing, performance validation, functional verification and documentation of configurations.
Final acceptance will be conducted only after successful demonstration of complete system functionality and
handover of all relevant documentation and credentials.

As part of the project deliverables, the NETS International will provide technical training for four (04) personnel
designated by the client organization. This training will focus on the operation, administration and maintenance

configuration management, troubleshooting techniques and best practices for network operations. Upon
successful completion of the training program, certification will be provided by the NETS International
associated with the deployed solution.
5.12 Support and Warranty
All supplied products under Phase 1 of the project will be covered by a minimum of three (3) years of
comprehensive OEM and NETS International support and warranty. This support will include technical
assistance, firmware updates and hardware replacement services as per OEM policies. The NETS International
will coordinate with the OEM to ensure timely resolution of any issues related to hardware or software
components.
UPS systems included in the project will be provided with one (1) year OEM and NETS International support and
warranty only. During the warranty period, the NETS International will provide technical assistance and
coordinate with the OEM for maintenance or replacement of defective components as required.
The NETS International shall also provide post-commissioning support services for at least one (1) year for

maintenance support to ensure smooth operation of the deployed systems.

The objective of this project is to install and deploy FortiGate 121G Next-Generation Firewall solution. The proposed
FortiGate 121G will provide enhanced network security, advanced threat protection, improved visibility and control,
secure VPN connectivity, resilient dual-WAN connectivity, and scalability to support the Habib Qatar's current and
future network requirements. The proposed solution will provide the required Next-Generation Firewall capabilities,
including stateful firewall inspection, application control, intrusion prevention, antivirus and anti-malware protection,
web and DNS security, botnet and Command-and-Control protection, threat intelligence, IP reputation and Geo-IP
filtering, DoS/DDoS protection, traffic monitoring, security logging and reporting, granular security policies, routing,
NAT/PAT, site-to-site VPN, remote-access VPN, and dual-ISP failover.
5. Scope of Work
NETS International Communications Ltd. will provide the complete supply, installation, configuration, commissioning,
and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) of the FortiGate 121G firewall. The scope will include physical installation, interface
and VLAN configuration, LAN/WAN connectivity, dual-ISP failover, routing, firewall policies, NAT/PAT, security profiles,
FortiGuard security services, site-to-site and remote-access VPN, logging and monitoring, configuration of the required
network and security parameters, functional testing, UAT support, and final handover of the implemented solution.

NETS International Communications Ltd. will supply the FortiGate 121G Next-Generation Firewall along with the
required hardware components, accessories, and applicable support subscriptions. The proposed solution will also
include the required licensing for secure remote access and VPN connectivity based on the agreed requirements. The
supplied FortiGate 121G will support the Habib Qatar's required security, networking and other requirements.
5.2 Installation and Deployment
NETS will perform the physical installation of the FortiGate 121G at the Habib Qatar's designated location. Installation
will include rack mounting where applicable, power connectivity, network interface connectivity, and initial hardware
verification. The FortiGate 121G will be connected to the Habib Qatar's existing network infrastructure.

NETS will configure the FortiGate 121G in accordance with the Habib Qatar's requirements and the approved
implementation design. Configuration will include the required LAN and WAN interfaces, VLANs, security zones,
routing, primary and secondary Internet connectivity, WAN health monitoring, automatic ISP failover, firewall policies,
NAT/PAT, application control, security profiles, logging and monitoring. The required site-to-site IPsec VPN and
remote-access VPN functionality will also be configured in accordance with the approved requirements. The
configuration will support applicable IKE versions, encryption, authentication, VPN tunnel monitoring and recovery
mechanisms.
5.4 Commissioning and Validation
NETS will commission the FortiGate 121G following completion of the installation and configuration activities.
Commissioning will include functional verification of firewall connectivity, security policies, Internet connectivity,
primary and secondary WAN links, automatic ISP failover, NAT/PAT, VPN connectivity, and security services. The
FortiGate 121G will be considered commissioned once the configured services have been tested and verified in
accordance with the agreed requirements. NETS will support the Habib Qatar during the final validation and handover
of the implemented solution.

8

NETS International Communications Ltd. will provide technical support for the implemented FortiGate 121G solution
during the agreed support period. Technical support will include assistance with configuration-related issues,
troubleshooting of firewall, network connectivity, and security policy-related issues. Non-critical issues will be
addressed remotely, while critical issues requiring physical intervention will be supported through onsite assistance.

Following successful commissioning, NETS will support the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) phase to validate that the
implemented FortiGate 121G solution meets the Habib Qatar’s operational and security requirements. UAT will
include testing of key functionalities such as Internet access, firewall policy enforcement, application control, VPN
connectivity, dual-WAN failover, and security services including IPS, web filtering, and malware protection.

The FortiGate 121G is an enterprise-grade Next-Generation Firewall offering up to 5.3 Gbps IPS throughput, 3.1 Gbps
NGFW throughput, and 2.8Gbps Threat Protection throughput with support for up to 3 million concurrent sessions. It
provides 16 × GE RJ45, 8 × GE SFP, and 4 × 10GE SFP+ interfaces, along with dedicated management and HA interfaces,
and 1x 480GB SSD internal storage for local logging, event storage, reporting, and packet capture, making it suitable
for secure, high-performance enterprise network environments.

The primary objective of this document is to define the technical requirements for the one-year support renewal
of Huawei routers. The renewal aims to ensure uninterrupted operation, timely support and continued reliability
of the existing network infrastructure across all deployed locations.
5. Scope of Work
The scope of services defines the overall support framework applicable to all covered assets under this renewal
period. The services are intended to ensure operational continuity, minimize downtime, maintain OEM-backed
support, operational stability and timely resolution of hardware and software-related issues during the contract
period. All services shall be delivered in accordance with Huawei standard support policies and entitlements linked
to the applicable part numbers for the deployed Huawei NetEngine AR651 routers.

The support renewal includes Huawei OEM hardware replacement services for the covered devices. In the event
of a verified hardware failure, Huawei shall provide repair or replacement of defective components in accordance
with the applicable Return Material Authorization (RMA) process and standard service levels.
5.2 Technical Assistance Center (TAC) Access
Authorized access to Huawei Technical Assistance Center (TAC) shall be provided for fault logging, incident
management, remote diagnostics and issue resolution. TAC support will be available through official Huawei
support channels throughout the support period.

The renewal entitles software maintenance support, including access to bug fixes, maintenance releases and
software patch recommendations relevant to the supported hardware models. Feature upgrades are subject to
Huawei entitlement terms.
5.4 Remote Configuration and Troubleshooting Guidance
Remote technical guidance shall be provided for configuration verification, troubleshooting and recovery
assistance during incidents. This service is limited to advisory support and does not include full network
reconfiguration or design changes.

On-Demand/On-site support, operational maintenance and professional services required during the support
period shall be provided by NETS International as part of their service responsibility. These services are outside
the OEM (Huawei).
5.6 Escalation and Case Management
Critical incidents shall be managed through Huawei’s escalation framework, ensuring priority handling, structured
case ownership with standard SLA definitions.

All OEM support services under this renewal shall remain valid for a period of one (1) year, aligned with the defined
renewal start and end dates and strictly applicable to the listed part numbers, quantities and serial numbers only.

7.1 Datacenter Facility & Environment Management
The Datacenter Infrastructure Specialist shall be responsible for comprehensive datacenter facility and
environment management, including managing critical infrastructure such as power systems (UPS and
generators), cooling systems (CRAC/CRAH and in-row cooling units), PDUs and structured cabling. The Specialist
shall continuously monitor environmental parameters including temperature, humidity, airflow and load
distribution while ensuring that the physical infrastructure complies with recognized industry standards and
organizational policies.

Under server room and rack management, the Specialist shall oversee the design and arrangement of racks,
servers, network equipment and storage arrays. The role includes maintaining accurate documentation of rack
layouts, asset inventories, patching diagrams and ensuring proper power and cooling load balancing within the
racks.

In terms of preventive and corrective maintenance, the Specialist shall conduct regular preventive maintenance
of UPS systems, batteries, cooling units, fire suppression systems and associated electrical gear. The Specialist
shall also coordinate repairs, replacements and vendor engagements for defective or malfunctioning
components to ensure uninterrupted operations.

For power and cooling optimization, the Specialist shall monitor power utilization effectiveness (PUE) and
ensure efficient cooling distribution across the facility. The role includes planning and implementing
improvements to reduce energy consumption, eliminate hot spots and enhance overall operational efficiency.
7.5 Security & Compliance
With respect to security and compliance, the Specialist shall ensure the physical security of the datacenter
premises through proper access controls, surveillance oversight and authorization mechanisms. The Specialist
shall also ensure compliance with safety standards, standard operating procedures (SOPs), audit requirements
and manufacturer guidelines.

In incident management and troubleshooting, the Specialist shall respond promptly to datacenter-related
incidents such as power failures, temperature alarms, UPS bypass events and other infrastructure disruptions.
The role includes conducting root cause analysis and implementing corrective measures to minimize downtime
and prevent recurrence.

The Specialist shall also provide infrastructure support for IT operations, including support to server, storage and
network teams during routine operations and project deployments, while ensuring the availability, reliability and
continuity of datacenter services.

text:
8.1 Daily Operational Support
The Datacenter Infrastructure Support Assistant shall provide daily operational support by assisting in
monitoring temperature, humidity, power loads, UPS alarms, cooling performance and other environmental
parameters. The role includes conducting routine walkthroughs of the datacenter and server rooms to identify
abnormalities and report any irregularities to senior personnel.

In equipment handling and rack assistance, the Support Assistant shall assist in the installation, removal and
relocation of servers, network devices, storage units and rack accessories. The Assistant shall also support
labeling, patching and organizing of cabling and power connections in accordance with defined procedures and
instructions.

For preventive maintenance support, the Assistant shall help in scheduling and coordinating maintenance
activities related to UPS systems, batteries, cooling units, generators and other electrical infrastructure
components.
8.4 Incident & Alarm Response
Under incident and alarm response responsibilities, the Assistant shall immediately notify senior staff regarding
UPS alarms, cooling failures, power fluctuations, or abnormal temperature readings. The Assistant shall provide
first-level troubleshooting support under the supervision and guidance of senior datacenter personnel.

Regarding physical security compliance, the Support Assistant shall monitor visitor access to ensure entry is
restricted to authorized personnel and vendors only, while ensuring adherence to all datacenter safety and
security rules.
8.6 Vendor & Team Coordination
The Support Assistant shall also coordinate with vendors for scheduled maintenance, inspections and equipment
deliveries and provide necessary support to IT teams during deployments, system testing and hardware
replacement activities.

The objective of this project is to replace the end-of-support routers deployed at Pakistan International Airlines
Corporation Limited (PIA)’s with Core Edge Routers. The proposed solution shall provide reliable, secure, and
scalable network connectivity between the internal data center infrastructure and external networks while
supporting advanced routing, WAN connectivity, redundancy, and traffic management capabilities. The project
shall also ensure migration and replication of the existing router configurations, integration with the current
network environment, and operational readiness of the deployed solution.
5. Scope of Work
The scope of work encompasses the supply, delivery, installation, configuration, migration, commissioning, testing,
and support of Core Edge Routers for PIA’s Data Center and Disaster Recovery Site.
5.1 Supply and Delivery
NETS shall supply and deliver six new Core Edge Routers, including the required hardware, power supplies,
software, and applicable licenses necessary for installation, configuration, and migration.
5.2 Installation of Routers
NETS shall perform the physical installation of the routers at the designated Data Center and Disaster Recovery
Site locations. The installation shall include rack mounting, power connections, network and fibre connectivity,
installation of required transceivers and accessories, and initial hardware verification. NETS shall ensure that the
routers are installed in accordance with OEM recommendations and PIA’s infrastructure requirements.
5.3 Configuration and Commissioning
NETS shall configure and commission the routers in accordance with PIA’s network architecture and operational
requirements. The configuration shall include the migration and replication of existing router configurations onto
the new equipment, along with the required routing protocols, IPv4/IPv6 routing, DHCP services, NAT, VPN
capabilities, and WAN connectivity features supported by the proposed routers.
NETS shall configure the required features, including VRRP, BFD, and hot standby, and other specified traffic
management capabilities. For the two designated routers, NETS shall configure the SD-WAN functionality,
including the applicable intelligent traffic steering and supported SD-WAN features. NETS shall integrate the new
routers with PIA’s existing network environment, validate interoperability, and commission the

NETS shall provide three years of onsite on demand hardware warranty support. The support arrangement shall
include the required three-year OEM Co-Care Premier Support for all routers and applicable software support and
critical updates in accordance with the relevant OEM entitlement. NETS shall provide technical assistance for issues
related to the supplied equipment, configuration, patch updates, software upgrades.

NETS shall conduct functional and operational testing to verify the configuration, connectivity, routing
functionality, and integration of the new routers with PIA’s existing infrastructure. Testing shall include validation
of the configured routing protocols, IPv4/IPv6 connectivity, redundancy mechanisms, WAN, and applicable traffic
management features.

The primary objective of this project is to ensure a seamless migration from the existing switch platform to a
modern Cisco switching infrastructure with minimal disruption to ongoing operations. This includes supply,
installation, configuration of new switches and migration of legacy switches, ensuring smooth transition and
integration into the PMRC’s network environment. Full functionality will be validated through systematic testing
and commissioning, ensuring that the deployed infrastructure meets all operational requirements. Additionally,
the project will include the safe dismantling and relocation of the old switches within the network racks to
maintain a structured and optimized network infrastructure.
The project supports future scalability and meet the growing demands of enterprise-grade services. By adhering
to industry best practices the project will deliver a robust, secure and future-ready network infrastructure that
supports PMRC’s long-term business objectives.
5. Scope of Work
The scope includes to migrate PMRC’s legacy switches to a new Cisco switch platform with minimal downtime
while ensuring standardized deployment, configuration and seamless integration into the existing network. NETS
International will also provide three (3) years of first-level support to maintain operational stability and will handle
the proper dismantling, relocation and organization of old switches within the network racks.
NETS International will be responsible for the end-to-end execution of the following services under this scope:

NETS International will be responsible for the supply and timely delivery of all required Cisco switches and
associated accessories, ensuring that the hardware meets PMRC’s technical and operational requirements.
Additionally, all supplied equipment would be OEM-certified and covered under standard manufacturer warranty.
5.2 Installation and Configuration
The installation and configuration phase will ensure that the new Cisco switches are deployed in a structured,
secure and fully optimized manner. NETS International will begin with the physical installation, which includes
racking of new switches in the designated network racks, ensuring proper power connectivity in compliance with
industry standards.
Following installation, the team will carry out initial configuration of the switches based on PMRC’s network design
and operational requirements. This configuration will include creating and assigning VLANs for segmentation,
updating firmware, configuring access ports for end-user devices and trunk ports to integrate seamlessly with the
existing infrastructure. Secure remote management features such as SSH, SNMPv3 and role-based access control
will also be configured to align with PMRC’s IT policies.
5.3 Testing and Commissioning
Once installation and configuration are complete, rigorous testing and commissioning of the new switches will
be performed. This will include validation of port connectivity, link aggregation, throughput and failover
mechanisms. The performance testing will ensure that the new hardware meets the required service-level
benchmarks.

8

NETS International will carefully undertake the migration of services, users and devices from the existing legacy
switches to the newly deployed switches. This will involve the safe dismantling and relocation of old switches
within the racks while minimizing downtime. A structured migration plan will be followed to ensure business
continuity during the transition and all critical services will be verified post-migration.

NETS International shall implement advanced security features on the new switches to strengthen the PMRC’s
network posture. This includes Access Control Lists (ACLs), port security, DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP
inspection, 802.1X authentication and any other applicable security mechanisms. Management access will be
secured using encrypted protocols and integrated with the PMRC’s existing monitoring and security systems.

The objective of this project is to replace SIEHS’s existing wireless infrastructure with a modern wireless networking
solution based on Wi-Fi 7 access points and the compatible management platform. The proposed solution aims to
improve wireless connectivity, network performance, coverage, security, and ease of management across the
deployed environment.
The project will include the supply and deployment of access points configuration of the wireless network, testing,
user acceptance testing (UAT), technical support, and final documentation and handover. The solution will be
implemented in accordance with the requirements.
5. Scope of Work
5.1 Supply and Delivery
NETS will supply and deliver 14 Huawei Ekit Wi-Fi 7 access points, along with the compatible management platform
and associated items included in the approved bill of quantities. All equipment will be delivered to the SIEHS-
designated location.
5.2 Installation and Deployment
NETS shall perform physical installation and mounting of the access points, connection to the existing network
infrastructure, physical labelling, and establish connectivity required for deployment. Installation will be
coordinated with SIEHS to minimize disruption to ongoing operations.
5.3 Configuration and Commissioning
NETS will configure and commission the proposed wireless solution using the compatible management platform
and supported product capabilities. Activities will include device onboarding, SSID and wireless security
configuration, radio configuration, and access point management.

NETS will provide three years of on-site on-demand technical support for the supplied and deployed equipment,
which includes troubleshooting configuration issues, and resolving wireless connectivity faults. The equipment is
backed by comprehensive 3 years OEM warranty and support, featuring Next Business Day (NBD) RMA for
hardware replacements.

NETS will conduct UAT with the SIEHS technical team after installation, and commissioning. Testing will verify
access point connectivity, wireless client association, SSID availability, authentication, connectivity, roaming,
management platform visibility, and network performance. The results will be documented in a UAT report. Issues
identified within the agreed scope will be addressed before final acceptance. UAT will validate delivered
functionality and will not establish compliance with excluded or unsupported features.
5.6 Documentation and Handover
NETS will provide equipment inventory, relevant product documentation, UAT results, and support and escalation
details. Formal handover will take place upon completion of the deployment, testing, and documentation
activities.

The objective of this proposal is to provide the State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan with a
comprehensive and secure end-to-end Network Security and Operational Performance Optimization services,
supported by dedicated on-site Resident Engineers for one year, extendable to two years. This engagement aims
to provide State Life with a skilled and experienced Resident Network Engineers to conduct a comprehensive
review of the current network design, validate it against industry standards and best practices and identify any
architectural flaws, misconfigurations, or performance bottlenecks.
It further seeks to optimize overall network performance by proactively identifying bottlenecks, enhancing
system reliability, improving traffic flow and ensuring the efficient operation of all network components including
firewalls, switches, routers and access points. The deployment of skilled Resident Engineers is intended to ensure
operational continuity through timely troubleshooting, routine maintenance, configuration updates and rapid
incident response. This initiative also aims to improve network visibility, maintainability and compliance while
ensuring knowledge transfer and close collaboration with State Life’s internal IT team.

5. Scope of Work
The scope of work includes a comprehensive assessment and optimization of the State Life existing network
infrastructure. A qualified network engineer will review the current network design and configuration to ensure
alignment with industry standards and best practices. This involves identifying and documenting any design
flaws, performance bottlenecks, or misconfigurations. The engineer will troubleshoot ongoing network issues,
perform root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to improve network performance, security and
reliability. The engagement will conclude with updated documentation and a knowledge transfer to the State
Life IT team.

The engineer will perform a detailed examination of the current network topology, including architecture,
hardware components, configurations and documentation to understand the existing setup and operational
flow. All device configurations will be reviewed to evaluate the scalability of the network, effectiveness of
VLAN segmentation, security mechanisms and redundancy implementations. The alignment of the design with
business continuity and operational needs will also be assessed.
All existing network documentation will be reviewed for completeness, accuracy and relevance, ensuring it
aligns with the actual deployed environment and facilitates future troubleshooting or upgrades.

8

The gap assessment will focus on identifying VLAN segmentation issues that hinder communication between
VLAN zones, including missing or misconfigured inter-VLAN routing policies. Any configuration gaps or design
flaws such as insufficient ACLs, overly simplistic firewall rules, or outdated settings will be documented, with
attention to their impact on both security and network performance.
Risk analysis will also be performed to highlight vulnerabilities like single points of failure, ineffective zoning
strategies, or outdated design practices. A prioritized set of recommendations will be provided, covering
improvements to VLAN tagging, enhancements to inter-VLAN routing and the implementation of stronger, zone-
based security measures based on key findings.

5.3 Troubleshooting
The engineer will investigate network performance issues, specifically network outages, latency, VLAN
communication challenges, misrouting by analyzing logs, configurations and network behavior that impact user
productivity or business operations. The troubleshooting process will be conducted in coordination with the
internal IT team to ensure accurate identification and validation of underlying issues, by the implementation of
effective and permanent fixes. Coordination with the internal IT team will be done to validate that all issues
have been resolved and that services are functioning as expected.

5.4 Rectification and Optimization
Based on the findings, the engineer will implement approved updates to firewall policies, switching
configurations and routing tables, with a focus on resolving the reported issues and aligning the setup with best
practices. The engineer will fine-tune network configurations to maximize performance, strengthen security
posture and improve overall network resilience.

9

continuity and serving as a single point of contact for network-related issues. The key responsibilities include:
6.1 Documentation and Reporting
The responsibilities include maintaining up-to-date documentation of network topology, configurations and
assets, while ensuring all incidents, changes and resolutions are recorded in a structured format. The role also
involves preparing and submitting daily, weekly, or monthly operational reports as required. Additionally,
support is provided in preparing audit and compliance documentation, along with managing relationships with IT
vendors and service providers, including OEMs, ISPs and support partners.

The Resident Engineer will be responsible for opening, managing and tracking support tickets. The role also
involves coordinating RMA processing, managing license renewals and handling any required service escalations
to ensure issues are addressed effectively and on time.
6.3 Incident Management & Troubleshooting
The Resident Engineer will manage incident logging and response using the designated ticketing system, perform
first-level troubleshooting for routine issues and escalate complex problems to the appropriate internal or

major or repeated incidents and documented. RCA findings will be shared with stakeholders. Furthermore, the

The objective of this project is to supply, install, configure, commission and support a resilient and high-
performance Data Center Core Switching solution for State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan (SLIC) Data
Center, Karachi. The proposed solution shall provide a reliable, scalable and low-latency network core capable of
supporting the Corporation’s existing and future IT infrastructure requirements. The solution shall enhance the
availability, performance and scalability of the Data Center network through high-capacity Layer 3 switching,
redundant architecture, advanced routing and data-center networking capabilities. The implementation shall also
provide the required security, and network management features to ensure efficient and controlled operation of
the Data Center core. NETS shall provide the complete solution on an end-to-end basis, including hardware supply,
delivery, installation, configuration, testing, commissioning, OEM support, local technical support and knowledge
transfer to the SLIC network team.
5. Scope of Work
The scope of work encompasses the end-to-end supply, delivery, installation, configuration, testing,
commissioning, and three-year comprehensive maintenance and support of the Data Center Core Switches at State
Life Insurance Karachi Data Center.
5.1 Supply and Delivery
NETS shall supply and deliver two (02) enterprise-grade Data Center Core Switches suitable for deployment within
the SLIC Data Center environment. The proposed solution shall provide high-capacity switching and forwarding
performance with sufficient high-speed interfaces to support the required server, network and uplink connectivity.
The supplied solution shall include all necessary components, transceivers, power supplies, fan modules, licenses
and associated accessories required for complete and operational deployment.

NETS shall perform the complete installation, configuration, integration, testing and commissioning of the supplied
core switching solution at the SLIC Data Center in Karachi. The configuration shall include the required Layer 2 and
Layer 3 services, routing, VLANs, VRF, management, QoS and traffic-management features in accordance with the
SLIC requirements. Following configuration, NETS shall conduct testing to verify connectivity, routing, management
and overall operation of the implemented solution. Any observations identified during commissioning shall be
addressed prior to handover.

Upon completion of installation, configuration and commissioning, NETS shall conduct User Acceptance Testing
(UAT) in coordination with the SLIC technical team. The UAT shall verify the functionality, connectivity,
performance, redundancy and management operation of the deployed core switching solution against the agreed
requirements. Following successful completion of UAT, NETS shall support the commissioning and handover
process and provide the relevant implementation and configuration information to SLIC.

OEM will provide support for the supplied solution in accordance with the requirements. The support shall include
the applicable hardware warranty, software support, software updates and upgrades, and access to the OEM
Technical Assistance Center (TAC) on a 24x7 basis. The support arrangement shall include advance hardware
replacement with same-day replacement where applicable.

8

NETS shall provide technical support for the supplied solution throughout the three-year support period. Technical
support shall be available 24x7 on-site on-demand for hardware faults, configuration issues, connectivity
problems, firmware/software requirements and other technical matters related to the supplied core switching
infrastructure. Critical incidents shall be coordinated with the OEM support organization through the applicable
escalation mechanism to facilitate timely resolution.

NETS shall provide technical training and knowledge transfer to the designated SLIC network team covering
administration, configuration, monitoring, troubleshooting and management of the implemented core switching
solution. The training shall enable the SLIC technical team to effectively operate and maintain the deployed
infrastructure following project completion and handover.

NETS shall provide the relevant technical documentation upon completion of the implementation. The
documentation shall include the implemented configuration, connectivity information, relevant addressing and
VLAN details, management information, and applicable warranty and support information. Final handover shall be
completed following successful commissioning and UAT.
